summary: A well that pieces of a few cells fall into on their own as time passes. Each move is one piece come to lie: turned and moved sideways while it falls, then dropped. Every row filled from side to side vanishes and what was above it moves down. The game ends when a piece has no room; a level may ask for so many rows within so many pieces. Played by the realtime loop, not by a kit: the loop reads the well and asks the rules and the solver where each piece goes.

cells.looks: a cell in the well's background colour
a block of a piece come to lie; the colour carries no rule
a cell hidden by a notice or an animation

state_fields.board: the well's rows from the top, each a list of cells from the left: 0 empty, 1 filled, null a cell nobody read; the falling piece is not on it
state_fields.piece: the piece to place now as its [row, column] cells shifted so its top-left is 0, 0; null when none is in play
state_fields.next: the coming pieces the game shows (its preview), first first, each as piece is; empty when it shows none
state_fields.score: the rows cleared (the game's own score is not kept)
state_fields.scene: the id of the scene the screen shows

actions.description: turn the falling piece to one of its shapes, move it to a column and drop it

scenes.looks: the well with a piece falling in it
a notice over the well that the game or the level is over

meta_actions.description: start another game after the end

preview.description: how many coming pieces the game shows

garbage.description: rows the simulated game begins with at the well's floor, each full but for one cell

goal_lines.description: rows a level asks to clear; null when it asks none or it is not known

goal_pieces.description: pieces a level gives to clear them in; null when it sets no limit or it is not known

pieces.description: the pieces the simulated game deals from: "tetromino" (the seven of four cells), "pentomino" (the eighteen of five), "small" (one to four cells); a real game's pieces are those seen coming
